Industries

Secure the land you answer for, from the air

Pipelines, concessions, servitudes and project footprints have one thing in common. Someone is answerable for what happens on land they cannot watch every day. We give those teams a dated, reviewed record of what stands on it, and of what has changed.

Request a proposal See sample outputs

Core industries

Where a dated register changes decisions

Pick the page for the land you manage. Each sets out the problems in your team’s own words, the services that answer them, what you receive and the country rules that shape the survey.

Pipelines · plants · field sites

Oil & gas

Pipeline rights of way and protection zones, new and rehabilitated cross-border lines, LNG host areas and their corridors, well pads and asset handovers. Usually starts with a register of the structures within the distances you choose, each measured to the line, with every 500 m rated for encroachment density.

Read

Concessions · tailings · expansions

Mining

Concession edges, tailings and hazard zones, expansion footprints and mineral-sands mine paths, surface excavations and rehabilitation. Usually starts with the structures inside and around your right, and a register of the structures inside your hazard zones.

Read

Line servitudes · bulk water · dams

Power & utilities

Transmission and distribution servitudes and wayleaves, vegetation management, new lines and cross-border interconnectors, bulk water mains and dams. Usually starts with a servitude register for each line segment.

Read

Lenders · monitors · consultancies

Project finance & ESIA

Resettlement cut-off dates, ESIA and RAP baselines, periodic monitoring for lenders’ reports and land due diligence. Usually starts with a dated register of the structures in the footprint on the cut-off date, fixed in an evidence pack.

One method, four vocabularies

The same question, asked in different words

Oil & gas: right of way and protection zones

Integrity and land teams ask which structures sit inside the right of way or the statutory protection strip, how close each is to the line, and what is new since the last patrol. Around plants, well pads and LNG sites the question is the same, measured against a safety zone.

Mining: concession edges and hazard zones

Tenure, social-performance and closure teams ask what is being built at the concession edge, which structures sit inside the zones engineers have drawn around tailings or blasting, and what the ground looked like before an expansion.

Power & utilities: servitudes and wayleaves

Servitude and line-maintenance teams ask what has been built under or beside the line, which stretches to clear or engage first, and how many structures each route option for a new line would affect.

Project finance & ESIA: baselines and cut-off dates

Lenders, independent monitors and ESIA or RAP teams ask what stood in the project footprint on the cut-off date, what has appeared since, and whether a grievance about a single location can be checked against dated imagery.

Local law, local language

Every industry page summarises the protection strips, servitude widths, regulators and drone rules that shape the survey, with the sources linked, and our country sites across Africa set out the local rules in local terms. Reports for Mozambique can be delivered in Portuguese.

Across every industry

What stays the same

Land and assets, not people

We map structures, cleared ground, excavations and tracks. Whether a structure is authorised is for you and the authorities to decide.

A person reviews every result

Automatic detection proposes and a reviewer decides. Anything the imagery cannot settle is listed for a ground check.

Dated, credited, delivered as files

Every report names its imagery and date where the source gives one, and arrives as a PDF and GIS files your teams already use.

Frequently asked questions

Our industry is not listed. Can you still help?

Probably. The method works for any linear asset or boundary where it matters what stands within a set distance, and when it appeared. Ports, industrial estates and land banks use the same register. Send the route or boundary and tell us what the record is for.

Do you work for contractors and consultants as well as asset owners?

Yes. EPC contractors, ESIA and RAP consultancies and independent monitors commission registers and GIS layers for their own deliverables, and we deliver in the formats their teams use.

Can we see work you have done in our industry?

We never publish a client’s route, imagery or results without written permission. The sample outputs on this site come from a high-pressure gas pipeline in Mozambique, shown with the route owner’s permission. For other industries we can run a labelled demonstration on a boundary or route you choose, from open data.

Which countries do you work in?

Satellite-based surveys need no site visit and no drone flight, and are offered through our country sites across Africa, listed on where we work. Drone surveys are subject to the approvals and security clearances each job requires, and each industry page sets out the country rules that shape the survey.

Know what stands inside your right of way, before it becomes a dispute.

Send us your route or site boundary and the distances that matter to you. We reply with a scope, an imagery plan and a written proposal.
